CAD prototype · 2026-10-07 · source pinned

Asimov upper body.
A smaller balancing base.

A fresh integrated model: original Asimov upper-body geometry and inertials on a new frame with 160 mm wheels. The rejected body layouts are discarded.

The load path, combined center of mass, wheel torque and arm motion are connected in one model. It remains a review prototype: hardware interfaces, thermal ratings and procurement are unresolved.

Cost is unquoted. Neither a $100, $200 nor $500 complete build is supported. Green blocks are declared allowances. Wheel shapes are envelopes.

What the tests actually show

At the assumed 6 Nm per wheel and floor friction μ=0.6, the 3D model recovers tested 2°, 5°, 10° and 15° leans. These research recoveries bypass the narrower candidate C fault guard and may exceed normal travel speed. With manual parking supports it stays upright without motor torque. Unparked power loss reaches 45° in roughly 0.85 seconds after the cut.

Fixed-body feedback drifts about 421 mm during the slow arm reach. Joint-dependent COM feedback reduces final drift to about 0.16 mm in simulation. The combined drive/turn/reach test stays balanced and tracks heading but misses its 30 mm path criterion by 4.37 mm at eight seconds.

Where it can break or lose balance

An assumed 12 mm shaft and 6 mm deck fail the selected structural margins. The model uses 14 mm and 8 mm, with conditional calculated margins. Clamp friction, preload, welded material properties and the source pelvis case capacity still require physical proof. Two full-range shoulder-yaw poses intersect source meshes. Low traction and excessive control delay cause recovery failures.

Software that needs to change

The shipped biped policy must be replaced or bypassed in a dedicated wheeled mode. This package contains an independent compiled balance core, an articulated COM-feedback experiment, exact source serial codecs and a review-only FOC patch for torque control, independent wheels and reduced command lag. Local IMU/encoder drivers, sensor fusion, deterministic scheduling, torque calibration and a supported fault/parking state machine are not yet implemented on hardware.
